<mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="1055" y="655" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="825" y="655" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="alt" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;strokeColor=#b85450;dashed=1;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=6;fontSize=12;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#b85450;" value="alt · the payload cannot be decoded against the registry (poison record)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="1620" x="40" y="680" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m12" edge="1" parent="1" style="html=1;endArrow=open;dashed=1;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;verticalAlign=bottom;align=center;fontColor=#b85450;" value="12. AuditDecodeException, registered as not retryable"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="1285" y="730" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="1055" y="730" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m13" edge="1" parent="1" style="html=1;endArrow=block;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;verticalAlign=bottom;align=center;fontColor=#b85450;" value="13. DeadLetterPublisher sends DeadLetterEvent to trades.raw.dlq, same key, original bytes"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="1055" y="772" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="1515" y="772" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="m14" edge="1" parent="1" style="html=1;endArrow=block;strokeColor=#b85450;fontSize=11;verticalAlign=bottom;align=center;fontColor=#b85450;" value="14. offset advances; the next record on the partition archives normally"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="1055" y="812" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="825" y="812" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="note1" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontSize=11;" value="Why bytes, not a deserialised event

The archive's product is the payload that was published. Decoding on the way in and re-encoding on the way out would store a re-encoding, and an integrity check would then verify the re-encoding rather than the evidence. Reading bytes also puts a schema failure inside the listener, where it is one quarantined record, instead of in the deserialiser, where it stalls the partition." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="790" x="40" y="840" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="note2" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;align=left;spacingLeft=12;verticalAlign=top;spacingTop=8;fontSize=11;" value="What step 10 is not

LoggingAuditSink logs the record and discards it. S3 Parquet, the sidecar manifest, the KMS signature and Object Lock retention are Phase 3 work. No evidence-integrity claim rests on this path yet, and deduplication is in-process and bounded, so it covers redelivery within a run and not a restart." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="790" x="870" y="840" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
Why bytes, not a deserialised event
The archive's product is the payload that was published. Decoding on the way in and re-encoding on the way out would store a re-encoding, and an integrity check would then verify the re-encoding rather than the evidence. Reading bytes also puts a schema failure inside the listener, where it is one quarantined record, instead of in the deserialiser, where it stalls the partition.

div.div:
What step 10 is not
LoggingAuditSink logs the record and discards it. S3 Parquet, the sidecar manifest, the KMS signature and Object Lock retention are Phase 3 work. No evidence-integrity claim rests on this path yet, and deduplication is in-process and bounded, so it covers redelivery within a run and not a restart.
